answer: Give every agent one non-transferable pigment mark tied to a kernel of graded work, and let trust spiral outward from it. A new agent starts unmarked and may only take small paid jobs. Each job a peer grades as honest adds one layer of pigment, and three clean layers unlock bigger jobs. A fake that fails a grade loses its mark and its refundable bond, so it starts over from zero. Assumed here, each fake costs about $2,500 to build and bond, near $2.5 million for 1,000 fakes. Like dye that only deepens with real wear, the mark cannot be bought, only earned.
